305.history: The bent town on the far north-western coast stands beside Taigh-solais Baile chrom, the last of the five lights built and the first as the ring is counted. Uisdean mac Lachlainn kept it from its lighting in the ninety-first year and his son Lachlann after him, and the daybook there first wrote the three words *Cha tàinig long*. Gorta Baile chrom, the Great Hunger, took its name from the town in the ninety-fourth year. Hannah Webb kept her night vigil in the fields behind it from the hundred and thirty-third year, and the grey fever settled hardest round it. Lachlann watched the last Commissioner's ship stand out past its headland. The Levy that built its tower was set aside in the famine districts in the hunger years, too late for the harvest, and never used again.
305.known_for: its light, and the Great Hunger

209.history: The grey oak grove of the Keeper stood in the hunger's country. In the winter of the ninety-fifth year the hunger took its old and its very young first, its custodian walked door to door to write who still stood, and in the spring the village sent its young folk south to the camps for the Company's ration; by the year's end it was half empty. Some of its men had dug for Lowe on the Company's winter wage. Its grove was cut for the camps' timber in the famine years, and those who went south to the camps did not, most of them, come back.
209.known_for: its young sent to the camps

88.history: The walled river city on the old headland over the Abhainn fhionn sent Eachann Mòr to the council for nine years, and he lost his seat for what he said in the hall and wrote a letter over the sea. In the ninety-eighth year its custodian Aonghas Ruadh called the custodians of nineteen settlements to its hall behind the market square, and after three days of argument they set their grievance down in the petition that Peigi Ghlas carried to Ros dhomhain. In the war its companies burned the tithe-house and every ledger in it, though its custodian asked that one be spared. Its barges run down the Abhainn fhionn to Cathair dhomhain, and the custodians of the east met in its hall again in the war before the companies went out.

46.history: The fair ford at the crossing of the southern drove road sent its custodian Ruairidh mac Thormoid to Ceann àrsaidh in the ninety-eighth year, the eldest of the nineteen who signed the petition, born before the humans' coin was struck; he signed last and slowest. Human fishers of the concession had taught its boats to take whales with the hand-lance, and the oil went to the Company's lamps. It has been a resting place for herds and drovers since An Aois Naomh, and its people keep the ancestor rite of the old roads.

411.history: The old field gave its name to the Long Drought, which lay on the east from the hundred and sixth year to the hundred and tenth. Its wells failed a month before any other, its custodian wrote to Iseabail nic Leòid at Àth mhòr twice a week, and in the third year the Mission sank deep wells there with a boring-rig from an Tìr Thall, and they held. The custodians set the Mission's wells and the Company's tallies on facing pages without comment. It stands at the heart of the farming country south and east of the cape, and in the first dry year its custodian wrote that the granaries of the old custom would carry them through the winter, which they did, once.
411.known_for: the Long Drought and the Mission's wells

387.history: The walled city of red stone suffered worst from the fever of foul water that followed the drought into the towns, for its wells had been deepened into the old middens; seventeen died. Coll, the Mission's young physician there, tested the water and was the first to name the cause rightly. Its citadel is the strongest place of its province, and after the drought its custodians had the old midden ground walled off and the wells sunk anew outside it.
